title: The Scenic Route
mood: On the bell tower a girl bites her lollipop and takes the scenic route up into the storm.

hero.alt: Close on Selena's face, black claws over her mouth and a sly smile in her red eyes; then, seen past her heels, a woman with long pink hair and floating fiery blades stands far ahead on a broken, frozen plain.

segs.t: Selena crouched on the wet tiles of the bell tower with her claws hooked over the edge. From up here the street at the mouth of the cut was small again. She did not look for anyone in it.
She had come back up for her own reasons. It stood high and clear over the Academy’s roofs. The storm hung low enough above it to split. And it was where she had always done her thinking.
The recall still burned in her cells. All day it had said one thing.
Come back.
Since the street, it also said where.
Before, the pull had run into the ship and spread out among the hanging blocks, and she had lost it there. Now it ran through the blocks to one place, deep inside, and ended.
She stopped pushing it away. She listened to it instead.
She followed it back, pulse by pulse, the way she followed a fault through a circuit on the workshop bench. One hall, deep in the ship. Someone stood in it.
The road ran straight back to its sender. Nobody had closed it.
Sloppy,
she thought, and was pleased with herself.
She spoke to the signal, since it was listening.
“Sorry, but I still prefer life at the Academy. Still, if you really want me to choose...”
The lollipop in her cheek was worn to a sliver. She always let them melt.
This one she bit. It cracked between her fangs.
She raised her head. The corners of her mouth lifted.
She took a deep breath. Arcs of electricity split the clouds above her and opened a path toward the Storm Citadel, the target of her ambitions.
“Even on the path to destruction, I’m taking the scenic route!”
Lightning swallowed her, and the clouds closed over.
The Storm Citadel.
Obsidia watched the lightning climb.

She saw it through the eyes of an Ender in the lowest towers. Minutes ago, through the four Enders at her pawn’s back, she had seen the pawn stand in front of the humans in its own shape. Then she had sent the last call, the one that carried where she stood.
Now it was coming up the road she had left open. In the lightning she could see its face. Defiance, and a will that did not bend.
Perhaps the finest thing she had made could tell her what came after, for her kind.
She felt a pleasure she had not known in a very long time.
“Look at how much you’ve grown, my child,” she said, to no one.
Her voice stayed perfectly calm. The violet in her eyes burned brighter than it ever had.
Along the line of her call, the hanging blocks slid apart.
The scenic route went straight up through the Citadel’s storm.

Black blocks hung upside down around her, every edge sharp. In their open holds gray Enders stood in rows and did not move. The blocks moved out of her way, one after another, and closed again behind her.
Through a tear in the storm, far below, the bell tower was the size of her hand. In the flooded wards the small lamps had stopped moving. Every one pointed up.
She slipped through a gap between two black ribs and landed in the throne hall.
It was dark and very large. Wide stairs ran up from where she stood into violet light.
At the top stood the throne, a column of joints lit violet from inside. It hummed.

media.alt: Seen past Selena's long blonde hair, wide dark stairs climb to a jointed column lit violet, a small figure waiting at its foot.

segs.t: The hum came down the stairs to meet her. She felt it in her heels. Under the ship’s deep note ran a lower one. She had heard it from the tower, just before the lights went out. Here it all came from one place.
So that’s where you keep the field,
she thought.
It was also the huntress’s seat.
A woman stood at the foot of it with her back turned. Long hair, gold running into pink. A gown of black and magenta. Red gloves that ended in claws.
Selena had never seen her. Her blood knew her anyway.
The huntress.
The recall had stopped burning. She had come where it wanted her.
The woman looked back over her shoulder. Her face was smooth shell with a cold sheen, and her eyes burned violet. Nothing in it was surprised. She had known Selena would come.
She turned all the way round.
“It has been a while, my little doll.”
Selena came up the stairs with her hands loose at her sides. At the top she gave her maker the brightest smile she had.
“It’s been a while, my dear creator.”
She did not remember a single minute of the last time.
“Remind me,” said Selena. “I never caught your name.”
“Obsidia.”
Selena tried it once in her head.
Obsidia.
Her maker came to her slowly. Nothing in this hall could hurry her.
She put out one gloved finger and set it under Selena’s chin. She tipped the face up into the violet light and looked it over, the way someone admires a thing she carved herself.

media.alt: Obsidia, pink and gold hair, looks down at Selena and holds her chin up with one red-gloved finger; Selena, small red horns in her blonde hair, looks back without a smile.

segs.t: Checking her work,
thought Selena.
Under that finger her blood went quiet, and wanted to stay quiet. She noted that, and filed it.
“Destruction gives rise to new life,” said her maker. “That is the meaning of purification.”
Selena stepped out from under the finger. She strolled round behind her maker with her hands clasped at her back. It put her between her maker and the seat.
She spun on her heel.
“Ah... so what should I destroy next?”
It was the line a good pawn would say. She said it like a joke, and watched to see how far it would get her.
Her maker turned her head. Her eyes narrowed.
“A pawn with no surprises left, of course.”
Wrong answer,
thought Selena.
She doesn’t want a yes.
Behind her, something scraped on the stone.
Chains of bone were crawling up out of the floor at her back, joint after joint, each one ending in a spike. Her maker smiled. She did not once look at the chains.
“Oh?” said Selena.
The chains coiled round her ankle, then her waist, and lifted her off the floor. They pinned her arms to her sides. She could not move.
The points rose toward her neck, slowly, one at a time.

media.alt: Bound in jointed chains of bone, Selena hangs high against the tall column while Obsidia floats below her, long weapon in hand, fiery blades hovering at her back.

segs.t: Her maker came round in front of her and looked up into her face.
“Savor your final moments, my dear Selena.”
Selena had picked that name herself. In her maker’s mouth it sounded owned.
The nearest point came to rest against her throat. It was cold.
Her maker never glanced at it. She watched Selena’s face, and waited.
Me, I hold the strings.
Selena had told the rain as much once, and believed it.
Now she hung in the air on someone else’s.
Her arms were pinned. Her hands were not.
She closed her claws round the nearest point and tore it apart.
Then Selena lifted her eyes to her maker’s. There was no yes in her face. It was a declaration of war.
“I’ll never be your puppet again!”

blocks.caption: I’ll never be your puppet again!

segs.t: Lightning burst out of her. The chains went to pieces and rattled away down the stairs.
Told you,
she thought.
Pull a leash too tight, and it snaps.
Her true form closed over her. Plate, white and blue and gold. A large pale mane. Four black-and-gold blades hung in the air around her, and a blade of crackling light ran along one arm.
It was the suit she had once shown the whole class, turning above her desk.
Ender plating, my own design.
Nobody had asked whose.
She had never let all of it out before. It fit.
Obsidia looked her over, the whole of it, slowly.
Selena had copied every face she had ever met. She knew what this one showed. It was close to pleasure.
She had not expected that.
“You’ve grown, Selena,” said Obsidia.
“Did I surprise you?”

media.alt: Lightning bursts from Selena's dark armor and tears the chains apart; plates and claws close over her face; Obsidia, close, smiles; then Selena stands in a storm of blue light in her full armor of white, blue and gold, blades floating around her.

segs.t: Obsidia did not answer. Her long silver-pink weapon was already in her hand.

Selena went in close. Obsidia gave ground down the stairs without hurry and kept her at the length of that weapon. At the lift of one finger it lashed out across the hall to meet Selena’s blade. Where they met, the hall flashed white. Obsidia fought as if she had all the time in the world.
Selena pressed, and the weapon drove her back. Step by step it drove her up the stairs, until her back struck the throne.
The hum came through her plates. The field’s hum. Her blood went quiet at it, the way it had under the finger. It wanted to stay quiet.
The seat was right above her. She could climb it now and take Obsidia’s place. Days before, on the tiles, she had thought she would, if she had to.
And then what?
she thought.
Sit in this hum for good, quiet as a good piece. Same board. Better chair.
She turned and cut the throne through at the base with the blade on her arm.

media.alt: Selena, in armor of white, blue and gold, stands at the foot of the tall dark column as glowing red cuts split it at the base.

segs.t: It came apart into pale plates and fell in a heap. She kicked pieces of it at Obsidia, one after another.
Deep in the ship something exploded. Then something else. Through the gaps between the ribs the clouds slid sideways. The whole Storm Citadel began to tilt, as if to fall.
Under her boots, the hum stopped.
